    • Here’s a sample of the data sent via the webhook:jsonCopy code{ "id": 123, "username": "newuser", "email": "newuser@example.com", "membership": "Premium" }
    • This data is processed by Zapier, and a message is sent to your Slack channel: “A new Premium member has joined: newuser@example.com”.

This process ensures you stay updated in real time, without manually checking the WordPress dashboard.

lessons.title: 💳 3. Advanced Payment Workflows
lessons.content:
If your membership site has complex payment needs (e.g., handling refunds, failed payments, or prorated upgrades), using the MemberPress API in combination with third-party payment processors like Stripe or PayPal can streamline operations.

Example: Automating Failed Payment Retries with Stripe API

Let’s say you want to automatically retry failed payments after a certain period (e.g., 3 days) and notify the user when a payment succeeds after a retry.

Steps:

  1. Set Up a Webhook for Failed Payments:
    • MemberPress can notify you via webhook when a payment fails.
    • Use this event to call the Stripe API and schedule a retry.
  2. Create an API Call to Retry Payments:
    • Once you receive the failed payment webhook, call the Stripe API’s payment intent retry feature:
      curl https://api.stripe.com/v1/payment_intents/pi_123456789/confirm \ -u sk_test_key: \ -d "payment_method"="pm_card_visa"
  3. Notify the User Upon Success:
    • If the retry is successful, send a notification email via your preferred email marketing API (e.g., MailChimp or ActiveCampaign).

This kind of automation ensures that your billing workflow is efficient, reducing the number of lost memberships due to failed payments.

lessons.title: 🔐 4. Implementing Single Sign-On (SSO)
lessons.content:
If you run a corporate membership site or one that requires seamless access across multiple platforms, implementing Single Sign-On (SSO) allows users to access MemberPress using existing credentials (like Google, Microsoft, or Facebook logins).

Example: Implement SSO with OAuth 2.0

Steps:

  1. Set Up an OAuth Server:
    • Use a service like Auth0 to manage user authentication and grant access tokens using OAuth 2.0.
  2. Modify MemberPress Authentication:
    • Customize the login process to authenticate users against your OAuth server. This can be done by hooking into WordPress's login system.
    Here’s a simplified version of what the code might look like:
    function custom_sso_authenticate($user, $username, $password) { $response = wp_remote_post('https://auth.your-oauth-server.com/token', array( 'body' => array( 'client_id' => 'YOUR_CLIENT_ID', 'client_secret' => 'YOUR_CLIENT_SECRET', 'grant_type' => 'password', 'username' => $username, 'password' => $password ) )); $response_body = wp_remote_retrieve_body($response); $data = json_decode($response_body, true); if (isset($data['access_token'])) { // Authenticate user in WordPress based on OAuth token } } add_filter('authenticate', 'custom_sso_authenticate', 10, 3);
  3. Authenticate Users:
    • Users can now log in using their existing credentials from your OAuth provider (e.g., Google or Microsoft), which simplifies the login experience and provides better security.

lessons.title: 📊 5. Custom Reporting Dashboards
lessons.content:
Advanced users often need custom reports and dashboards that go beyond the default MemberPress reporting. By combining MemberPress API data with a visualization tool like Google Data Studio or Tableau, you can create live dashboards that display membership trends, revenue data, and more.

Example: Visualizing Member Growth in Google Data Studio

Steps:

  1. Pull Data from MemberPress API:
    • Create a scheduled script that pulls membership data from the API and sends it to Google Sheets: GET https://your-site.com/wp-json/mp/v1/members
  2. Connect Google Sheets to Data Studio:
    • Import the Google Sheets data into Google Data Studio to create custom reports and charts.
  3. Create Dashboards:
    • Build interactive charts to display metrics like monthly active members, new subscriptions, churn rate, and lifetime value (LTV).

This approach gives you a visual, at-a-glance view of your membership site’s performance without needing to manually download data.

sections.title: 📚 Advanced Concepts for MemberPress API and Integrations

lessons.title: 🔗 1. WordPress Plugin Development and Customization
lessons.content:
To help you advance in your API and integration journey, here are some in-depth topics and resources to expand your knowledge. These readings focus on advanced customization, security, and integration techniques for MemberPress, WordPress, and third-party tools.

If you're looking to extend MemberPress through custom plugins, understanding WordPress's plugin development lifecycle is essential. This enables you to create custom API endpoints, modify plugin behavior, and add advanced features to your membership site.

  • Reading: WordPress Plugin Handbook
    • The official documentation on building WordPress plugins, covering hooks, filters, and REST API integration.
  • Related Theme: Using WordPress hooks to extend MemberPress functionality with custom actions and filters.

lessons.title: 🛡 2. Securing Your REST API
lessons.content:
Security is critical when dealing with sensitive membership data, such as emails, payment information, and user subscriptions. Learning about best practices in securing REST APIs will help you protect your site from vulnerabilities.

  • Reading: REST API Security Essentials
    • An in-depth guide to REST API security, including authentication techniques (OAuth, JWT, API keys) and preventing common attacks (e.g., CSRF, injection).
  • Related Theme: Implementing OAuth 2.0 or JWT (JSON Web Tokens) for securing MemberPress REST API requests in custom apps.

lessons.title: 🌐 3. Extending OAuth 2.0 for Single Sign-On (SSO)
lessons.content:
For enterprise-level membership sites, implementing Single Sign-On (SSO) can improve the user experience by allowing members to log in with external accounts (e.g., Google, Facebook). OAuth 2.0 provides the framework to enable SSO across platforms.

  • Reading: OAuth 2.0 and OpenID Connect in Plain English
    • A beginner-friendly guide that simplifies the complex concepts behind OAuth 2.0 and OpenID Connect, providing examples of how to integrate them into your WordPress site.
  • Related Theme: How SSO improves security by using trusted identity providers, reducing the need for additional logins.

lessons.title: 🛠 4. Advanced API Automation with Zapier and Integromat
lessons.content:
Connecting MemberPress to other platforms via Zapier or Integromat allows you to automate workflows across apps without writing complex code. These tools are especially useful when integrating MemberPress with CRMs, email marketing platforms, or payment processors.

  • Reading: Zapier Automation Guide for Membership Sites
    • A practical guide on automating common tasks like sending email notifications, updating CRM records, or triggering marketing campaigns using Zapier workflows.
  • Related Theme: Automating billing cycles, member upgrades, or cancellations through Zapier and MemberPress webhooks.

lessons.title: 📊 5. Data Visualization and Reporting with Google Data Studio
lessons.content:
If you’re interested in creating custom reports and dashboards for tracking membership data, Google Data Studio provides a powerful tool for visualizing MemberPress API data. This allows you to track KPIs like monthly revenue, active memberships, and subscription trends in real time.

  • Reading: Visualizing API Data with Google Data Studio
    • A detailed guide on connecting Google Sheets and APIs to Google Data Studio for real-time data reporting.
  • Related Theme: Integrating MemberPress API data with external Google Sheets or Tableau to create custom analytics dashboards.

lessons.title: 💳 6. Advanced Payment API Workflows
lessons.content:
Handling payments is central to any membership site. Learning how to integrate payment gateways (like Stripe, PayPal, and others) with the MemberPress API can help you automate complex payment workflows such as refunds, subscription upgrades, and payment retries.

  • Reading: Stripe API Documentation
    • Official documentation for Stripe’s API, detailing how to manage payments, subscriptions, and refunds programmatically.
  • Related Theme: Handling failed payments through automated retries and sending notifications to members using a combination of MemberPress and Stripe webhooks.

lessons.title: 🔐 7. JWT (JSON Web Tokens) for Securing API Communication
lessons.content:
JWT is a widely used method for securely transmitting data between parties as a JSON object. This is particularly useful for securing REST API communication between your site and external services, ensuring that only authorized users can interact with your MemberPress API.

  • Reading: JWT.io Introduction to JSON Web Tokens
    • A beginner's guide to JWT, explaining how tokens work, how to secure APIs with JWT, and use cases for authentication and authorization.
  • Related Theme: JWT versus API keys for securing REST API requests and improving authorization mechanisms in MemberPress.

lessons.title: 📧 8. Integrating Email Automation with APIs (MailChimp, ActiveCampaign, etc.)
lessons.content:
Email marketing and automation are key components of member retention and engagement. By integrating MemberPress with email marketing platforms, you can automate welcome sequences, renewal reminders, and upselling based on member behavior.

  • Reading: MailChimp API Documentation
    • Learn how to integrate MailChimp with your membership site using API calls to automatically segment users, send campaigns, and track engagement.
  • Related Theme: Member segmentation and automated email triggers based on user actions (e.g., upgrading subscriptions, missing payments, or completing courses).

lessons.title: ⚙️ 9. Custom Webhooks for Advanced Workflows
lessons.content:
Webhooks allow you to create real-time notifications and integrations with other services when events happen in MemberPress (e.g., new member signups, cancellations, or subscription upgrades). You can trigger workflows or send notifications based on these events.

  • Reading: What Are Webhooks and How Do They Work?
    • A beginner-friendly explanation of webhooks, their purpose, and how to set them up for membership-related workflows.
  • Related Theme: Using MemberPress webhooks to trigger external services (e.g., notifying a CRM, updating Slack, or logging user activity in an analytics system).

lessons.title: 🖥️ 10. WordPress REST API Customizations
lessons.content:
In some cases, the default WordPress REST API might not cover all the functionality your site needs. Learning how to extend the WordPress API can help you expose additional data or create custom API endpoints for handling unique membership workflows.

  • Reading: Customizing the WordPress REST API
    • A technical guide on adding custom endpoints to the WordPress REST API, allowing you to fetch or modify data beyond the standard API offerings.
  • Related Theme: Creating custom API endpoints for specialized workflows, such as pulling user activity stats or automating advanced subscription modifications.

sections.title: 🧪 Tests and Simulations: Creating Custom API Endpoints, Testing OAuth Workflows, and Advanced Payment Automations

lessons.title: 1. 🔧 Creating Custom API Endpoints
lessons.content:
Let's dive into some hands-on tests and simulations! We’ll cover:

  1. Creating custom API endpoints in WordPress for MemberPress.
  2. Testing OAuth 2.0 workflows for secure API authentication.
  3. Building advanced payment automations using Stripe.

These examples will help you extend your site's functionality, secure your API, and automate complex payment flows.

MemberPress relies on the WordPress REST API. You can extend the default capabilities by adding custom API endpoints to handle specific workflows, such as retrieving member statistics, accessing premium content, or modifying user data.

Example: Create a Custom API Endpoint to Retrieve Active Members

Steps:

  1. Create a Custom Plugin:
    • In your WordPress installation, create a new plugin to add custom API functionality.
    • Go to wp-content/plugins/, and create a folder called custom-memberpress-api. Inside that folder, create a file named custom-memberpress-api.php.
  2. Add the Following Code: <?php /* Plugin Name: Custom MemberPress API Description: Adds custom API endpoints to retrieve active members. */ // Register the custom API endpoint on plugin activation add_action('rest_api_init', function() { register_rest_route('custom_mp/v1', '/active-members', array( 'methods' => 'GET', 'callback' => 'get_active_members', 'permission_callback' => '__return_true', )); }); // Define the callback function that returns active members function get_active_members() { global $wpdb; $active_members = $wpdb->get_results("SELECT * FROM {$wpdb->prefix}members WHERE status = 'active'"); return new WP_REST_Response($active_members, 200); }
    • This code defines a new REST API route: /wp-json/custom_mp/v1/active-members.
    • The get_active_members() function retrieves all active members from the WordPress database and returns them in the response.
  3. Activate the Plugin:
    • Go to your WordPress admin dashboard, navigate to Plugins, and activate the "Custom MemberPress API" plugin.
  4. Test the Custom Endpoint:
    • Use Postman or cURL to test your new endpoint.
    • Send a GET request to: https://your-site.com/wp-json/custom_mp/v1/active-members

Expected Response:

You should receive a JSON response listing all active members:

[
    {
        "id": 1,
        "username": "john_doe",
        "email": "john@example.com",
        "status": "active"
    },
    {
        "id": 2,
        "username": "jane_doe",
        "email": "jane@example.com",
        "status": "active"
    }
]

Customization Ideas:

  • Add Parameters: You could extend the endpoint to allow filtering by membership levels or dates, such as retrieving members who joined in the last 30 days.
  • Permissions: Replace __return_true with a custom permission callback to ensure only authenticated users can access the endpoint.

lessons.title: 2. 🔐 Testing OAuth 2.0 Workflows for Secure API Authentication
lessons.content:
OAuth 2.0 is one of the most secure methods for authenticating API requests, especially if you need to authorize third-party apps or external systems to interact with your MemberPress API.

Example: Implement OAuth 2.0 Authentication for the MemberPress API

Steps:

  1. Set Up an OAuth Server:
    • You can use an external OAuth provider like Auth0 or Keycloak to manage authentication tokens.
    • In this example, we’ll assume you’ve set up an OAuth provider (such as Auth0) and obtained a Client ID and Client Secret.
  2. Obtain an Access Token:
    • Use Postman to request an OAuth 2.0 token from your provider. Set up the following in Postman:
      • Method: POST
      • URL: https://your-oauth-provider.com/oauth/token
      • Body (form data): client_id: YOUR_CLIENT_ID client_secret: YOUR_CLIENT_SECRET grant_type: client_credentials
    • Click Send to obtain an access token.
  3. Make an Authorized API Request:
    • Now that you have an access token, you can use it to make authenticated requests to your MemberPress API.
    • In Postman or cURL, set the Authorization header:makefileCopy codeAuthorization: Bearer YOUR_ACCESS_TOKEN
    • For example, retrieve all members: curl -X GET "https://your-site.com/wp-json/mp/v1/members" \ -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_ACCESS_TOKEN"

Customization:

  • Token Expiration: Implement token expiration policies to ensure tokens expire after a specific period and can be refreshed using a refresh token.
  • Scope Management: Assign different scopes to tokens to control what parts of the API third-party applications can access (e.g., read-only access to member data).

lessons.title: 3. 💳 Building Advanced Payment Automations Using Stripe
lessons.content:
If you are using Stripe to manage payments for your membership site, you can leverage Stripe’s API to build advanced payment workflows. This could include handling failed payments, issuing refunds, or upgrading subscriptions.

Example: Automating Failed Payment Retries with Stripe

Steps:

  1. Set Up a Webhook for Failed Payments:
    • In your Stripe dashboard, create a Webhook that listens for payment events such as invoice.payment_failed.
    • Set the webhook to send a notification to a custom handler URL (for example, https://your-site.com/stripe-webhook).
  2. Handle the Webhook in WordPress:
    • In your WordPress installation, create a custom plugin or use the same one from earlier to handle Stripe webhook events: add_action('rest_api_init', function() { register_rest_route('custom_mp/v1', '/stripe-webhook', array( 'methods' => 'POST', 'callback' => 'handle_stripe_webhook', 'permission_callback' => '__return_true', )); }); function handle_stripe_webhook(WP_REST_Request $request) { $body = json_decode($request->get_body(), true); if ($body['type'] == 'invoice.payment_failed') { $customer_id = $body['data']['object']['customer']; // Logic to retry payment or notify the member } return new WP_REST_Response('Webhook received', 200); }
  3. Automate Payment Retry:
    • After receiving a failed payment event, you can use Stripe’s API to retry the payment: curl https://api.stripe.com/v1/invoices/inv_12345/pay \ -u sk_test_your_secret_key:
  4. Notify the User:
    • If the retry succeeds, notify the member by email or via a message on their account page.

Customization:

  • Automate Refunds: Use the Stripe API to automatically issue refunds for failed payments after multiple retries.
  • Notify Admins: Set up notifications in Slack or email to alert site admins when payments fail or when retries succeed.

title: MemberPress & Event Espresso for Non-profit Organizations
content:
Welcome to "MemberPress & Event Espresso for Non-Profit Organizations" 🎉

Are you part of a non-profit organization looking to streamline membership management and event planning? Whether you're managing recurring donations, organizing fundraising events, or engaging with your community, you know how challenging these tasks can be.

This course is designed to help you harness the power of two powerful WordPress tools—MemberPress and Event Espresso—so you can manage your memberships, create seamless event registrations, and maximize your fundraising efforts, all without technical hassle.

In this hands-on course, you will:

  • Learn how to set up MemberPress to manage memberships, collect recurring donations, and create exclusive content for your supporters.
  • Discover how Event Espresso can simplify event ticketing, automate attendee registrations, and help you run successful fundraising events.
  • See how these two tools can work together to offer personalized event experiences and boost member engagement.

Empower your non-profit with the right tools and strategies to grow your community, increase donations, and create meaningful impact. Let's dive into MemberPress and Event Espresso for non-profit organizations. I’ll break it down step-by-step and ensure it's easy to understand.

What are MemberPress and Event Espresso? 🛠️

  • MemberPress is a WordPress plugin that allows organizations to create membership sites, manage subscriptions, and restrict access to specific content based on membership levels.
  • Event Espresso is another WordPress plugin designed to handle event management, allowing organizations to sell tickets, register attendees, and manage events.

Both tools are particularly useful for non-profits because they simplify managing memberships and events, key activities for many organizations in this sector.

How Non-Profits Benefit from These Tools 🎯

1. Membership Management with MemberPress

  • Fundraising and Donations: Non-profits can use MemberPress to create membership tiers, each with its own set of benefits, making it easier to collect recurring donations.
  • Exclusive Content: Nonprofits can increase engagement and incentivize higher levels of giving by offering exclusive content or reports for donors or members.
  • Community Building: MemberPress integrates well with community tools like forums or discussion boards, fostering communication and engagement among supporters.

2. Event Management with Event Espresso

  • Event Registration: Non-profits often hold fundraising events, workshops, or charity galas. Event Espresso simplifies the ticketing and registration process, allowing attendees to register online.
  • Ticketing and Payments: Event Espresso allows non-profits to sell tickets and accept donations during registration, streamlining fundraising efforts.
  • Tracking and Reporting: Event Espresso provides robust reporting features, which can be helpful for tracking attendance and financials.

Integrating MemberPress and Event Espresso for Non-Profits 🧩

Non-profit organizations can integrate MemberPress and Event Espresso for seamless management of members and event attendees. Here’s how this combination can be useful:

  • Discounts for Members: You can offer discounted or free event access to members using Event Espresso, with MemberPress managing membership validation.
  • Recurring Donations: Events can act as gateways for attracting new members, and you can use MemberPress to convert event attendees into recurring donors.
  • Automated Notifications: Both plugins allow you to automate notifications, sending out reminders to members about upcoming events or renewal deadlines.

sections.title: 🔼 Fundamental Concepts: Membership and Event Management for Non-Profits

lessons.title: 1. Membership Management 🌍
lessons.content:
What is Membership Management?

Membership management is the process of organizing and overseeing individuals or organizations who formally join a group. In non-profits, members may be donors, volunteers, or supporters who contribute in various ways.

Core Concepts:

  • Membership Tiers: Many non-profits offer different levels of membership (e.g., Bronze, Silver, Gold). Each tier can represent a level of financial contribution or participation.
  • Exclusive Content/Perks: To incentivize people to join or donate more, non-profits can offer exclusive content, newsletters, or special events to members.
  • Recurring Donations: Membership programs often use recurring donation models, where members contribute on a monthly or yearly basis.

Importance to Non-Profits:

Memberships provide a reliable income stream and help create a committed community around the organization's mission. Through effective membership management, non-profits can maintain engagement, build loyalty, and ensure sustained funding.

lessons.title: 2. Event Management 🎟️
lessons.content:
What is Event Management?

For non-profits, events serve as a powerful way to engage supporters, raise funds, and spread awareness about their cause. Managing events involves organizing, promoting, registering attendees, and handling logistics like ticketing and venue management.

Core Concepts:

  • Event Registration: Non-profits need a system that allows supporters to easily register for events online. This simplifies the process for both organizers and attendees.
  • Ticketing and Pricing: Event organizers may offer different ticket types (e.g., VIP, General Admission) and set pricing based on attendee categories, such as members vs. non-members.
  • Donations Through Events: Non-profit events are often tied to fundraising efforts, where attendees donate directly or participate in fundraising activities like auctions.

Importance to Non-Profits:

Events offer a direct way to raise funds and engage a broader audience. Effective event management helps non-profits build awareness, raise critical funds, and create lasting relationships with supporters.

lessons.title: 3. Combining Membership and Events 💼
lessons.content:
By linking membership and event management, non-profits can amplify their impact:

  • Incentivizing Memberships: Offering members discounts or exclusive access to events encourages more supporters to join as members.
  • Building Community: Events can act as meeting points for members, fostering a sense of community and shared purpose.
  • Recurring Engagement: Events provide ongoing touchpoints for non-profits to engage with their membership base, ensuring continued involvement and financial support.

lessons.title: 4. Technology as a Solution 💻
lessons.content:
In the digital age, tools like MemberPress and Event Espresso help streamline both membership and event management by automating many aspects of these processes. This means less manual work for non-profit staff and more time focusing on the mission.

  • Automation: Tools like MemberPress can automate membership renewals, notifications, and access to exclusive content.
  • Data and Reporting: Both platforms provide detailed analytics, helping non-profits track member activity, event attendance, and overall engagement.
  • Payment Integration: These tools easily integrate with payment gateways (like Stripe or PayPal), making it simple for non-profits to accept donations, membership fees, and ticket sales.

lessons.title: Summary of Key Concepts
lessons.content:
• Membership Management: Creating a structure for recurring support, organizing tiers, and offering exclusive perks.
  • Event Management: Organizing events that drive engagement and fundraising while efficiently handling logistics like registration and ticketing.
  • Integration: Using technology to streamline operations, create a seamless supporter experience, and amplify both membership and event impact.

sections.title: 💡 Examples and Metaphors: Membership and Event Management for Non-Profits

lessons.title: 1. Membership Management – The "Garden" Metaphor 🌱
lessons.content:
Think of your membership program as a garden. Each member is like a plant that needs care, attention, and nurturing to grow.

  • Basic Members: These are your small, blooming flowers—people who give a small, recurring donation. They may not have a lot of perks but are steady contributors.
  • Premium Members: These are your tall, sturdy trees—those who donate larger amounts, support the mission at a deeper level, and receive additional benefits like exclusive content or VIP access to events.
  • Exclusive Content as Water: Just as water nurtures plants, the exclusive content or benefits you provide to your members (e.g., newsletters, reports, or special webinars) keeps them engaged and motivated to continue their contributions.
  • Renewals and Communication as Sunlight: Consistent communication (email updates, reminders for renewals) is the sunlight that ensures members stay aware of the value they receive and the importance of their continued support.

With MemberPress, you can automate the watering (exclusive content) and sunlight (reminders) to ensure your garden continues to thrive!

lessons.title: 2. Event Management – The "Party Planner" Metaphor 🎉
lessons.content:
Imagine running a charity event like hosting a large party:

  • Ticket Sales: The tickets to your event are like party invitations. Some might be VIPs who get exclusive treatment (like a fancy dinner or special seating), while others have general access to enjoy the main activities.
  • Seating and Registration: When guests arrive at your party, you need to know who’s attending, what they’ve paid for, and if they have special needs. This is where Event Espresso comes in—like your digital party planner, it ensures everything from check-in to seating runs smoothly.
  • Fundraising Activities: During the event, you might have a fundraising activity, like a silent auction or a donation drive. Here, you can treat Event Espresso as your trusty “money box,” collecting donations from attendees in real-time.
  • Post-Event Follow-Up: After the party, you send thank-you cards (email notifications) to everyone who attended. You also keep track of who donated and how much, just like how Event Espresso helps you generate reports and thank attendees automatically.

In this metaphor, Event Espresso is your all-in-one party planner: selling tickets, organizing seating, handling donations, and making sure everything runs smoothly.

lessons.title: 3. Integration of Both – The "Clubhouse" Metaphor 🏡
lessons.content:
Imagine your non-profit organization as a clubhouse where members gather and events are held.

  • MemberPress: Think of MemberPress as the key to the clubhouse. Only members with a certain key (level of membership) can enter specific rooms. Some rooms are accessible to all members (basic content), while others are reserved for high-level supporters (premium content). The software ensures everyone has access to the right spaces based on their membership.
  • Event Espresso: Once inside the clubhouse, Event Espresso organizes all the events. Whether it’s a charity gala, workshop, or seminar, it’s the event manager that sets up the room, arranges seating, and collects ticket payments. It even sends out reminders to attendees so no one forgets when the event starts!

When combined, these two tools make your clubhouse a well-organized, vibrant space where members feel valued, and events run seamlessly.

lessons.title: 4. Real-Life Non-Profit Example – A "Wildlife Conservation Organization" 🦅
lessons.content:
Let’s say you run a non-profit dedicated to saving endangered wildlife.

  • MemberPress Example: You create membership tiers based on donation levels—such as "Eagle Supporter" ($10/month), "Wolf Protector" ($25/month), and "Bear Guardian" ($50/month). Each tier gets access to exclusive content like behind-the-scenes videos, annual reports, and live Q&A sessions with field experts. MemberPress handles all the renewals, donations, and access.
  • Event Espresso Example: You host an annual "Conservation Gala" to raise funds. Tickets are sold through Event Espresso, which tracks attendees, collects payments, and sends out event reminders. Attendees can choose from various ticket options (e.g., basic admission or VIP table) and donate further during the event.
  • Combining the Two: As a special perk, Bear Guardian members get discounted or free tickets to the gala, all managed automatically by integrating MemberPress and Event Espresso.

lessons.title: Summary of Metaphors
lessons.content:
• Membership as a Garden: Members need constant care (exclusive content, communication) to grow and thrive.
  • Event as a Party: Organizing an event is like hosting a party where Event Espresso ensures everything from invitations to donations runs smoothly.
  • Clubhouse: MemberPress controls access to exclusive rooms, while Event Espresso manages events inside the clubhouse.
  • Real-Life Application: Combining these tools allows non-profits like a wildlife organization to easily manage both memberships and fundraising events.

sections.title: 🧪 Real-World Simulation: Managing Memberships and Events for a Non-Profit

lessons.title: Step 1: Setting Up Membership Levels with MemberPress 🌱
lessons.content:
Scenario: You want to offer different membership tiers to raise ongoing donations for wildlife conservation.

Action Plan:

  1. Define Membership Tiers:
    • Eagle Supporter: $10/month – Access to exclusive blog posts and newsletters.
    • Wolf Protector: $25/month – All of the above, plus early bird access to events.
    • Bear Guardian: $50/month – All of the above, plus free admission to the annual gala and a personal thank-you gift.
  2. Set Up in MemberPress:
    • Go to the MemberPress Dashboard.
    • Create a new Membership Level for each tier: "Eagle Supporter," "Wolf Protector," and "Bear Guardian."
    • Configure the pricing for each level (monthly payments).
    • Define the access rules: Set what content or perks each membership tier can access. For example, Eagle Supporters get access to exclusive blog posts, while Bear Guardians get gala tickets.
  3. Automate Recurring Payments:
    • Connect MemberPress with a payment gateway (e.g., Stripe or PayPal).
    • Enable automatic renewals for memberships so donations continue without the member needing to manually renew.
  4. Member Sign-Up:
    • Customize the sign-up form to make it appealing. Highlight the perks of each membership tier.
    • Share the membership sign-up page on your website and through email campaigns to encourage people to join.

Result:

Your membership program is now up and running. New members can sign up, choose their tier, and have access to exclusive content depending on their level of support.

lessons.title: Step 2: Organizing an Event with Event Espresso 🎉
lessons.content:
Scenario: You’re hosting your annual “Wildlife Conservation Gala” to raise funds and bring supporters together.

Action Plan:

  1. Create an Event in Event Espresso:
    • Navigate to the Event Espresso Dashboard.
    • Create a new event titled “Wildlife Conservation Gala.”
    • Set the event date, time, and venue information (e.g., June 15, 2024, 7:00 PM, at the Local Nature Preserve).
  2. Define Ticket Types:
    • Create various ticket options:
      • General Admission: $50
      • VIP Admission: $100 (includes a special dinner and a meet-and-greet with conservationists).
    • Add discount codes for members:
      • Wolf Protectors get a 10% discount.
      • Bear Guardians get free admission (automatically applied using MemberPress integration).
  3. Enable Registration:
    • Customize the registration form to collect important information like dietary preferences for VIP attendees.
    • Set a limit on tickets (e.g., only 200 tickets available to keep the event intimate).
  4. Promote the Event:
    • Publish the event registration page on your website and share it through social media.
    • Use Event Espresso’s automated email system to send reminders and updates to registered attendees.

Result:

Your gala is now open for registration. Attendees can easily buy tickets, and your members get special access or discounts based on their membership level.

lessons.title: Step 3: Integration – Linking MemberPress and Event Espresso 🔗
lessons.content:
Scenario: You want to ensure that your members automatically receive discounts or free access to the gala based on their membership level.

Action Plan:

  1. Set Up Membership Discounts:
    • In Event Espresso, create discount codes or free access for specific membership levels.
    • Use the MemberPress integration to verify member status at the time of ticket purchase.
    • Automatically apply a discount code for Wolf Protectors or grant free tickets for Bear Guardians.
  2. Track Attendance and Membership:
    • Use Event Espresso’s reporting tools to see how many of your members have registered for the event.
    • If some members have not signed up, use the automated email reminder system in both MemberPress and Event Espresso to nudge them.

Result:

The integration ensures that members enjoy their perks seamlessly. Your gala is filling up with attendees, and you’ve strengthened your relationship with key supporters by recognizing their contribution with special access or discounts.

lessons.title: Step 4: After the Event – Reporting and Follow-Up 📊
lessons.content:
Scenario: You need to follow up with attendees and report the event’s success to your board and members.

Action Plan:

  1. Generate Event Reports:
    • In Event Espresso, pull a detailed report on the gala, including:
      • Total ticket sales
      • Funds raised through additional donations during the event
      • Attendance breakdown (general public vs. members)
  2. Member Engagement Reporting:
    • In MemberPress, review how many new members joined leading up to the event and how many existing members upgraded their membership.
    • Compare these figures to past months to measure the impact of the gala on membership growth.
  3. Send Follow-Up Emails:
    • Use Event Espresso to send thank-you emails to all attendees.
    • Send personalized follow-up emails to Bear Guardians who attended, thanking them for their commitment to wildlife preservation and offering them exclusive content as a token of gratitude.

Result:

The post-event follow-up is seamless. You’ve kept supporters engaged, shared the event's success, and have valuable data on how the event impacted membership and fundraising goals.

lessons.title: Summary of the Simulation
lessons.content:
By following this real-world simulation:

  • You set up a membership program in MemberPress, allowing you to create different donation tiers and automate ongoing support.
  • You organized a successful fundraising event with Event Espresso, making it easy for supporters to register, buy tickets, and donate.
  • The integration between MemberPress and Event Espresso allowed for seamless discount application and member validation at the event.
  • Post-event reporting helped you measure success and engage with attendees, ensuring continued support.

sections.title: 🔗 Deeper Look at Integration: MemberPress and Event Espresso for Non-Profits

lessons.title: Why Integrate MemberPress and Event Espresso? 🧩
lessons.content:
Let’s explore a deeper integration between MemberPress and Event Espresso, which can help your non-profit run smoother by automating processes and providing a seamless experience for both members and event attendees.

Integrating these two tools allows your non-profit to:

  • Offer event perks based on membership levels (e.g., discounted or free event access).
  • Automatically verify memberships when attendees register for events.
  • Create a unified experience for members, ensuring they feel recognized and valued.

With the integration in place, you don’t have to manually manage member privileges for events or cross-reference lists. Everything becomes automated and tied together, saving your team time and reducing the risk of human error.

lessons.title: Key Integration Features 🔑
lessons.content:
Member Discounts and Access Control:

  • Ensure that members get discounts or special access to events without needing manual intervention. For example, Bear Guardians can automatically receive free access to an event, while Wolf Protectors might get a 10% discount.

Automatic Membership Verification:

  • When a person signs up for an event using Event Espresso, the system automatically checks their membership status in MemberPress and applies relevant perks (discounts, free access, etc.).

Unified Payment System:

  • Both MemberPress and Event Espresso can use the same payment gateways (e.g., Stripe, PayPal), making it easy for non-profits to track revenue from both memberships and events in a single place.

Centralized Reporting:

  • You can combine membership data and event data to get a comprehensive report on overall engagement. For instance, you can see how many members attended your event, how much revenue was generated, and how many new members joined during an event promotion.

lessons.title: Integration Methods 🔧
lessons.content:
There are several ways to integrate MemberPress and Event Espresso. Below are two primary methods: using built-in tools or employing third-party connectors.

1. Direct Integration with Plugins and Built-in Tools

If you use both MemberPress and Event Espresso as WordPress plugins, the integration is mostly handled through settings and configurations within the platforms.

Steps for Direct Integration:

  1. Install Both Plugins:
    • Ensure that both MemberPress and Event Espresso are installed and activated on your WordPress site.
  2. Configure Membership Levels in MemberPress:
    • Create membership tiers in MemberPress (e.g., “Eagle Supporter,” “Wolf Protector,” “Bear Guardian”).
    • Define the rules for content access and event discounts for each tier.
  3. Create Events in Event Espresso:
    • Set up your event in Event Espresso with different ticket types (e.g., General Admission, VIP).
    • Under the pricing section, create discount codes or automatic price adjustments for members of specific tiers.
  4. Link MemberPress Memberships to Event Espresso:
    • Use the built-in features of both plugins to automatically apply discounts to members when they purchase event tickets.
    • Event Espresso will recognize active memberships in MemberPress, applying the correct discount based on membership status.
  5. Test the Integration:
    • Run tests by signing up as different members and purchasing tickets to verify that the correct discounts and free access are applied.

2. Using Third-Party Integration Tools (e.g., Zapier)

If you want to go beyond the built-in integration options or automate more complex workflows, you can use a tool like Zapier. Zapier allows you to connect different apps (including WordPress plugins) and automate specific actions.

Steps for Zapier Integration:

  1. Create a Zapier Account:
    • Sign up for a Zapier account if you don’t already have one.
  2. Connect MemberPress and Event Espresso to Zapier:
    • Use Zapier’s available integrations for MemberPress and Event Espresso.
    • Create a Zap (automation rule) where a new membership in MemberPress triggers an action in Event Espresso—for example, automatically sending an email with event registration details or discount codes to new members.
  3. Set Up Automation Rules:
    • Example #1: When someone purchases a new membership in MemberPress, Zapier can automatically create a corresponding discount code for them in Event Espresso.
    • Example #2: When someone registers for an event in Event Espresso, Zapier can automatically add them to a specific membership tier in MemberPress (e.g., converting one-time event attendees into ongoing members).
  4. Test Your Automations:
    • Run tests to ensure that when someone becomes a member, the correct event discount or access is provided without any manual steps.

lessons.title: Advanced Integration Scenarios 🚀
lessons.content:
Now that you have a solid understanding of the basics of integrating MemberPress and Event Espresso, let’s take it to the next level with advanced automations using Zapier. This will help your non-profit automate tasks that would otherwise take time and manual effort, creating a smoother experience for both your members and your event participants.

What is Zapier? 🤖

Zapier is a powerful automation tool that connects different apps and services without needing to code. In our case, we can use it to integrate MemberPress and Event Espresso beyond their native capabilities.

A Zap consists of:

  1. Trigger: An event in one app that starts the automation (e.g., a new member signup in MemberPress).
  2. Action: The automated response that happens in another app (e.g., creating a discount code in Event Espresso for that new member).

Let’s go through some advanced automation scenarios for your non-profit using these tools.

lessons.title: Benefits of Full Integration 🎯
lessons.content:
Integrating MemberPress and Event Espresso creates a unified system where your members and event attendees get a seamless experience, and your team gets powerful automation tools:

  • Efficiency: Manual processes like verifying memberships or applying discounts are automated, saving staff time and reducing errors.
  • Member Loyalty: Members feel valued when their perks are automatically recognized, making them more likely to stay engaged with your non-profit.
  • Growth Potential: Turning one-time event attendees into ongoing members becomes easier when you automate the transition through integrations.

sections.title: 🚀 Advanced Automation for Non-Profits: Integrating MemberPress and Event Espresso with Zapier

lessons.title: What is Zapier? 🤖
lessons.content:
Now that you have a solid understanding of the basics of integrating MemberPress and Event Espresso, let’s take it to the next level with advanced automations using Zapier. This will help your non-profit automate tasks that would otherwise take time and manual effort, creating a smoother experience for both your members and your event participants.

What is Zapier? 🤖

Zapier is a powerful automation tool that connects different apps and services without needing to code. In our case, we can use it to integrate MemberPress and Event Espresso beyond their native capabilities.

A Zap consists of:

  1. Trigger: An event in one app that starts the automation (e.g., a new member signup in MemberPress).
  2. Action: The automated response that happens in another app (e.g., creating a discount code in Event Espresso for that new member).

Let’s go through some advanced automation scenarios for your non-profit using these tools.

lessons.title: 1. Automatically Create Personalized Event Discount Codes for New Members 🎟️
lessons.content:
Scenario: Every time someone signs up as a member in MemberPress, you want to automatically create a personalized discount code for that member to use at an upcoming event in Event Espresso.

Steps to Automate:

  1. Trigger: A new membership purchase in MemberPress.
    • When someone signs up for a specific membership level, Zapier will recognize this and trigger the next action.
  2. Action: Create a discount code in Event Espresso.
    • Zapier automatically creates a unique discount code in Event Espresso based on the new member’s details.
    • This discount can be tailored based on their membership level (e.g., 10% off for “Wolf Protectors,” 50% off for “Bear Guardians”).
  3. Action: Send an email to the new member.
    • After the discount code is created, Zapier can send an email to the new member, giving them the discount code and encouraging them to sign up for the event.

Benefits:

  • No Manual Work: You don’t need to manually create and send discount codes; Zapier does this automatically when new members join.
  • Personalized Experience: Members receive personalized emails and exclusive event discounts, making them feel valued.

lessons.title: 2. Convert Event Attendees Into Members Automatically 🔄
lessons.content:
Scenario: After someone attends an event (using Event Espresso), you want to offer them an easy way to become a recurring member of your non-profit through MemberPress.

Steps to Automate:

  1. Trigger: Successful event registration in Event Espresso.
    • When someone registers for your event, Zapier is triggered by their completed registration.
  2. Action: Send a post-event email encouraging membership signup.
    • After the event, Zapier can automatically send an email inviting the attendee to join your non-profit’s membership program, with a special offer.
    • Example: "Thank you for attending the Wildlife Conservation Gala! As a special thank-you, we’d like to offer you a 20% discount on your first year of membership."
  3. Action: Automatically create a MemberPress account for them.
    • If they click the offer and sign up, Zapier can automatically create an account for them in MemberPress, assign them to the appropriate membership tier, and set up recurring payments.

Benefits:

  • Maximized Event ROI: By converting event attendees into ongoing members, you create a sustainable source of recurring donations.
  • Automated Follow-Up: You don’t need to manually track and reach out to event attendees; Zapier ensures each participant gets the opportunity to become a member.

lessons.title: 3. Notify Staff When High-Level Members Register for Events 📬
lessons.content:
Scenario: Whenever a VIP member (like your top-tier “Bear Guardians”) registers for an event, you want your non-profit’s team to be notified so that they can personally reach out and thank them.

Steps to Automate:

  1. Trigger: A VIP member registers for an event in Event Espresso.
    • When someone in the “Bear Guardian” membership tier signs up for an event, Zapier triggers the workflow.
  2. Action: Send an internal notification.
    • Zapier sends an email or Slack notification to your staff with details about the registration.
    • Example: "Alert: John Doe (Bear Guardian) has registered for the Conservation Gala. Consider sending a personalized thank-you note."
  3. Action: Add the member to a VIP guest list.
    • Zapier can also update a shared document or CRM (like Google Sheets or Salesforce) to add the VIP member to a specific list for special treatment at the event (e.g., ensuring they are seated at the VIP table).

Benefits:

  • Personalized Engagement: Staff can offer a personal touch to high-value members, increasing their loyalty and engagement.
  • Immediate Notifications: Important members get recognized and appreciated in real-time, strengthening their relationship with your organization.

lessons.title: 4. Offer Membership Upgrades After Event Attendance 📈
lessons.content:
Scenario: After a member attends an event, you want to offer them an exclusive opportunity to upgrade their membership level (e.g., from “Eagle Supporter” to “Wolf Protector”).

Steps to Automate:

  1. Trigger: A member attends an event in Event Espresso.
    • When a member registers for and attends an event, Zapier triggers based on their attendance status.
  2. Action: Send an upgrade offer.
    • After the event, send a personalized email offering them a discounted membership upgrade.
    • Example: "Thank you for attending our latest event! As a valued Eagle Supporter, we’d like to offer you an exclusive 25% discount to upgrade to Wolf Protector and enjoy additional benefits like early access to events."
  3. Action: Automatically upgrade their membership.
    • If the member accepts the offer, Zapier can automatically upgrade their membership in MemberPress and adjust their recurring donation amount accordingly.

Benefits:

  • Increased Member Engagement: Offering upgrades based on event attendance keeps members motivated to contribute more.
  • Revenue Growth: Upgrading members means more donations for your non-profit without the need for manual follow-ups.

lessons.title: 5. Track Event Engagement and Membership Conversions in One Dashboard 📊
lessons.content:
Scenario: You want to track how many members attend events, how many non-members join as a result of an event, and how much revenue is generated from events versus memberships—all in one place.

Steps to Automate:

  1. Trigger: Event registrations and membership signups.
    • Track all registrations in Event Espresso and membership signups in MemberPress.
  2. Action: Create a comprehensive dashboard.
    • Use Google Sheets or a CRM like Salesforce as your central tracking hub. Zapier can automatically send data from both Event Espresso and MemberPress to a shared document or dashboard.
    • Example: “John Doe registered for the Wildlife Conservation Gala (Event Espresso)” and “John Doe signed up for Bear Guardian membership (MemberPress).”
  3. Action: Visualize the data.
    • Use a tool like Google Data Studio to create real-time charts and reports on the data, showing:
      • How many members attended events.
      • How many event attendees became members.
      • Total revenue from memberships vs. events.

Benefits:

  • Data-Driven Decisions: You’ll have a clear picture of how events contribute to member growth and fundraising.
  • Centralized Reporting: With everything in one dashboard, you can easily report success metrics to your board and plan future events and membership strategies based on real data.

lessons.title: Summary of Advanced Automations
lessons.content:
These automations will allow your non-profit to:

  • Automatically create and apply personalized discounts for members.
  • Convert event attendees into recurring members.
  • Notify staff of high-value registrations.
  • Offer and automate membership upgrades after events.
  • Track member-event engagement in a single, comprehensive dashboard.

sections.title: 💡 Advanced Automation: Automatically Creating Personalized Discounts for Members in Event Espresso via Zapier

lessons.title: Scenario Overview 🎯
lessons.content:
Let’s dive deeper into how you can use Zapier to automatically create personalized discount codes for your members when they sign up through MemberPress. This automation will streamline the process of offering special event pricing to members without manual effort.

Scenario Overview 🎯

Whenever someone joins or renews a membership through MemberPress, you want to:

  1. Automatically generate a personalized discount code for an upcoming event managed through Event Espresso.
  2. Notify the new member with their discount code via email.
  3. Ensure the discount is appropriate for the membership level (e.g., a 10% discount for lower tiers, free tickets for higher tiers).

lessons.title: Steps to Set Up the Automation Using Zapier 🤖
lessons.content:
1. Set Up MemberPress as the Trigger

Trigger: A new membership purchase or renewal in MemberPress.

  1. Log into Zapier and create a new Zap.
  2. Set MemberPress as the Trigger App.
  3. Select the Trigger Event: “New Membership” or “Membership Renewed.”
  4. Connect your MemberPress account to Zapier by entering the necessary credentials.
  5. Choose the membership level(s) that will trigger the automation. For example, you might want to apply this only to members who join the “Wolf Protector” or “Bear Guardian” tiers.

2. Create Discount in Event Espresso

Action: Automatically create a personalized discount code in Event Espresso.

  1. After selecting MemberPress as the trigger, set Event Espresso as the Action App.
  2. Choose the Action Event: "Create Discount Code" (or similar, depending on the available actions in your integration).
  3. In the Create Discount Code step, configure the following:
    • Discount Code Name: Use a combination of the member’s name and the event name for a personalized feel (e.g., “JOHNDOE10”).
    • Discount Amount: Set the discount based on the membership level:
      • Wolf Protectors: 10% off
      • Bear Guardians: Free tickets
    • Validity Period: Define how long the discount code will be valid. You might limit it to a specific event date (e.g., valid for the upcoming “Wildlife Conservation Gala”).
    • Ticket Type: Specify which tickets the discount applies to (e.g., General Admission or VIP).

3. Send Discount Code to the New Member via Email

Action: Notify the new member with their personalized discount code.

  1. Set Gmail, Outlook, or any other email service as the next Action App (or use Zapier's built-in Email app).
  2. Create an email template that includes:
    • A personalized greeting with the member’s name.
    • A thank-you message for joining and supporting your non-profit.
    • The discount code generated in the previous step.
    • A call-to-action, encouraging them to register for the upcoming event using their discount.

Example Email Template:

Hi {{Member First Name}},

Thank you for joining our **Wolf Protector** membership! As a token of our appreciation, we’re excited to offer you a **10% discount** to attend our upcoming **Wildlife Conservation Gala**.

Here’s your personalized discount code: **{{Discount Code}}**

Use this code when you register at [Event Registration Link] to save on your ticket.

We look forward to seeing you there and continuing to work together to protect wildlife!

Best regards,
[Your Non-Profit Name]
  1. Configure Zapier to insert the discount code from the previous step into the email template automatically.

4. Test the Automation

Before going live, it’s essential to test the entire process:

  1. Run a test through Zapier:
    • Sign up for a new membership in MemberPress.
    • Verify that a new discount code is automatically generated in Event Espresso.
    • Ensure the discount code is sent via email to the new member.
  2. If the test is successful, the automation is working correctly. If something doesn’t work, check each step for errors or missing details.

lessons.title: Optional: Advanced Customization
lessons.content:
Member Tier-Specific Rules: You can use Zapier’s Filters to customize the automation further. For instance, set different rules for Wolf Protectors and Bear Guardians:

  • Wolf Protectors: 10% discount applied.
  • Bear Guardians: Free event tickets generated automatically (instead of a percentage discount).

Personalized Expiration Dates: You can dynamically set the discount code’s expiration based on the member’s join date or the event’s date.

lessons.title: Benefits of This Automation 🔑
lessons.content:
1. Time-Saving: No more manually creating discount codes or sending emails. Everything is automated, ensuring your team can focus on bigger tasks.
  2. Personalized Experience: Members feel valued because they receive exclusive, personalized discount codes tied directly to their membership.
  3. Consistency: Ensures that every member receives the right discount for their membership level, reducing the chances of errors or missed communications.

lessons.title: Summary of Steps
lessons.content:
• Step 1: Trigger the automation when a new membership is created or renewed in MemberPress.
  • Step 2: Automatically generate a personalized discount code in Event Espresso based on the membership tier.
  • Step 3: Send an email to the new member with their personalized discount code and event details.
  • Step 4: Test and go live.

sections.title: 🛠️ Step-by-Step Guide: Setting Up Automated Discount Creation Using Zapier 🤖

lessons.title: Getting Started
lessons.content:
Let’s walk through the process of setting up a Zap in Zapier that automatically creates a personalized discount code in Event Espresso when a new member joins via MemberPress. I’ll guide you step by step to ensure you can automate this workflow efficiently.

Step 1: Create a Zapier Account (If You Don’t Have One)

  1. Go to Zapier’s website and sign up for an account.
  2. Once signed in, click the Create Zap button in the upper-right corner.

Step 2: Set Up MemberPress as the Trigger

1. Choose the Trigger App

  • In the Trigger section, search for MemberPress.
  • Select it as the Trigger App.

2. Select the Trigger Event

  • Choose New Membership or Membership Renewal as the Trigger Event depending on whether you want this Zap to activate for new members only or for both new and renewing members.

3. Connect Your MemberPress Account

  • If this is your first time connecting MemberPress to Zapier, click Connect a New Account.
  • You’ll be prompted to enter your MemberPress API key. You can find this key in your MemberPress dashboard under the Developer settings.

4. Set Trigger Filters (Optional)

  • If you want the Zap to trigger only for certain membership tiers (e.g., only for Wolf Protectors or Bear Guardians), you can add filters in this step:
    • Click Filter Setup and specify the membership levels (e.g., "membership level is equal to 'Wolf Protector'").

5. Test the Trigger

  • After setting up the trigger, Zapier will pull sample data from your MemberPress account (like member names, membership levels, etc.) to ensure everything is connected properly. Run a test to make sure it's fetching the correct information.

Step 3: Set Up Event Espresso as the Action

1. Choose the Action App

  • In the Action section, search for Event Espresso.
  • Select it as the Action App.

2. Select the Action Event

  • Choose Create Discount Code (or similar) as the Action Event.

3. Connect Your Event Espresso Account

  • If you haven’t connected Event Espresso to Zapier before, click Connect a New Account.
  • Follow the prompts to log into your WordPress site and connect Event Espresso to Zapier. You may need to enable the Zapier integration add-on in your Event Espresso plugin if it’s not already installed.

4. Customize the Discount Code Settings

  • Discount Code: Create a dynamic discount code using the member’s name or a custom code, such as JOHNDOE10 or WILDLIFE10.
  • Discount Amount: Based on the member’s tier, set the discount percentage or amount:
    • Wolf Protector: 10% discount.
    • Bear Guardian: 100% discount (free tickets).
  • Expiration Date: Set an expiration date for the discount code if necessary, such as valid only for the next event or for a limited time (e.g., valid for 30 days).
  • Ticket Type: Specify which event or ticket type the discount applies to (e.g., General Admission, VIP).

Step 4: Send a Personalized Email to the New Member

1. Choose the Email App

  • In the Action section, click the + button to add another action.
  • Choose an email service (like Gmail, Outlook, or Zapier’s built-in Email tool) as the Action App.

2. Select the Action Event

  • Choose Send Email as the Action Event.

3. Customize the Email Content

  • To: Use the member’s email pulled from the MemberPress trigger.
  • Subject: Set a personalized subject line like "Welcome to Wildlife Defenders! Here’s Your Event Discount Code."
  • Body: Write a personalized message. Include the discount code generated from Event Espresso by pulling the Discount Code data from the previous step.

Example:

Hi {{Member First Name}},

Welcome to the **Wolf Protector** membership! As a thank you for supporting Wildlife Defenders, we’re offering you a **10% discount** on our upcoming event, the **Wildlife Conservation Gala**.

Your discount code is: **{{Discount Code}}**

Use this code at [Event Registration Link] to save on your tickets.

We look forward to seeing you at the event!

Best regards,  
The Wildlife Defenders Team

4. Test the Email

  • Run a test to ensure that Zapier sends an email to the member with the correct discount code from Event Espresso.

Step 5: Test Your Zap

Now that everything is set up, it’s time to test the full process:

  1. Run a Test Zap: Go back to your Zap dashboard and run a test from start to finish. Sign up as a new member in MemberPress.
  2. Check that a discount code is generated in Event Espresso.
  3. Verify that the member receives an email with the correct discount code and details.
  4. Check the discount in Event Espresso to confirm it applies to the correct event or ticket type.

Step 6: Activate Your Zap

Once you’ve tested the Zap and everything works smoothly, turn it on. Zapier will now automatically create discount codes and send personalized emails whenever a new member joins or renews through MemberPress.

lessons.title: Bonus: Advanced Customization Ideas
lessons.content:
1. Different Discounts for Different Membership Levels:
    • Use Zapier’s Filters to create different workflows based on the membership level.
    • Example: For Wolf Protectors, create a 10% discount, but for Bear Guardians, set the discount at 100% (free ticket).
  2. Add Dynamic Expiration Dates:
    • If you want the discount code to expire after a certain period (e.g., 30 days from membership signup), you can use Zapier’s date functions to dynamically set expiration dates based on the member’s join date.
  3. Use Zapier Multi-Step Zaps:
    • You can add additional actions to your Zap if needed, such as logging the discount code creation in a Google Sheet for internal tracking or sending a Slack notification to your team when a VIP member receives a discount.

lessons.title: Summary of Steps
lessons.content:
1. Set MemberPress as the Trigger for when a new member signs up.
  2. Set Event Espresso as the Action to create a discount code automatically.
  3. Send a Personalized Email to the new member with the discount code using Gmail, Outlook, or Zapier's Email tool.
  4. Test and activate the Zap to ensure everything runs smoothly.

sections.title: 📈 Examples: How Non-Profits Can Grow Through Technology Integrations 💻

lessons.title: 1. Donor Management & Personalized Engagement Using CRM Integrations
lessons.content:
Integrating technology into your non-profit’s operations can dramatically improve efficiency, engagement, and fundraising efforts. By combining various tools and systems, non-profits can streamline workflows, automate tasks, and focus more energy on their core mission.

Below are several examples of how non-profits can leverage technology integrations to grow:

Tools: Salesforce, HubSpot, Zapier

How It Works:

  • Salesforce or HubSpot can be used as a CRM (Customer Relationship Management) tool to track donations, interactions, and engagement with donors.
  • By integrating your website’s donation platform (e.g., Stripe, PayPal) with Salesforce or HubSpot, you can automatically update donor profiles with the latest donations and contact info.
  • Automating personalized email sequences using tools like Mailchimp or ActiveCampaign ensures that donors receive customized messages and updates based on their engagement history.

Example Growth Impact:

  • Personalized Engagement: When a donor gives a large gift, your CRM can automatically trigger an email thanking them for their contribution, followed by a personal call from your executive team. This personalized attention encourages future donations.
  • Lifecycle Tracking: You can automate follow-up messages at crucial moments (e.g., after a one-time donor makes their second donation, offer them a chance to become a monthly supporter).

lessons.title: 2. Automated Recurring Donations & Membership Renewals
lessons.content:
Tools: MemberPress, Stripe, Zapier

How It Works:

  • Use MemberPress to manage memberships and recurring donations on your non-profit’s website.
  • By integrating Stripe (or another payment gateway) with MemberPress, you can automate recurring donations. This ensures that donors don’t need to manually renew their contributions every month or year.
  • Zapier can be used to trigger personalized thank-you emails, reminders, or even exclusive member content based on their recurring donation activity.

Example Growth Impact:

  • Increased Retention: Automating renewals ensures that members don’t forget to donate again, increasing retention rates.
  • Seamless User Experience: Donors can manage their subscriptions, update payment details, or change membership tiers easily through an integrated platform, reducing churn.

lessons.title: 3. Fundraising Events & Ticketing Automation
lessons.content:
Tools: Event Espresso, Zoom, Zapier

How It Works:

  • Using Event Espresso, you can create events (virtual or physical) and sell tickets directly on your website.
  • Integrate Zoom for virtual events, so when attendees register via Event Espresso, they automatically receive Zoom links and access credentials for the online event.
  • Zapier can automate follow-up actions such as adding registrants to a Google Sheet, triggering personalized email campaigns, and providing post-event surveys.

Example Growth Impact:

  • Reduced Manual Labor: Automating the ticketing and registration process means fewer manual tasks for your team and a smoother experience for attendees.
  • Increased Attendance & Engagement: Personalized follow-up emails (e.g., sending additional content to attendees or offering future event discounts) keep participants engaged long after the event ends.

lessons.title: 4. Volunteer Management & Engagement Automation
lessons.content:
Tools: Volgistics, Mailchimp, Slack, Zapier

How It Works:

  • Volgistics is a volunteer management system that helps non-profits organize volunteer shifts, track hours, and communicate with volunteers.
  • By integrating Volgistics with Mailchimp, you can automate volunteer onboarding and engagement emails (e.g., sending training materials to new volunteers).
  • Integrating Volgistics with Slack ensures that team leaders are notified immediately when shifts are filled or when volunteers complete their tasks.

Example Growth Impact:

  • Increased Volunteer Retention: Automating the communication process (reminders, appreciation emails, training) keeps volunteers engaged, leading to higher retention rates.
  • Improved Coordination: Automated notifications in Slack help team leaders stay organized, allowing for more efficient use of volunteers’ time.

lessons.title: 5. Text Messaging Campaigns for Donations and Updates
lessons.content:
Tools: Twilio, Zapier, Stripe

How It Works:

  • Using Twilio, non-profits can send text message campaigns to donors and supporters, encouraging donations or providing updates on urgent campaigns.
  • Integrating Twilio with Stripe allows donors to make quick contributions by simply replying to the text message or clicking a link.
  • Zapier can link this process to your CRM (e.g., Salesforce), automatically updating donor records whenever a contribution is made.

Example Growth Impact:

  • Instant Engagement: Text messaging offers a direct and immediate way to reach donors. For example, a well-timed message during a disaster relief campaign can prompt immediate donations from supporters.
  • Seamless Donations: With one-click payment options, donors are more likely to contribute since they don’t have to navigate through a complex process.

lessons.title: 6. Advanced Analytics for Donor Behavior and Event Success
lessons.content:
Tools: Google Analytics, Salesforce, Google Data Studio

How It Works:

  • By integrating Google Analytics with your website and donation pages, you can track how visitors behave on your site—where they come from, how long they stay, and whether they complete a donation.
  • Salesforce can be used to track donor behavior and donation history, allowing you to identify trends or high-value donors.
  • Google Data Studio can aggregate data from these platforms to create a comprehensive dashboard that shows you the health of your fundraising campaigns, event success rates, and donor engagement metrics.

Example Growth Impact:

  • Data-Driven Decisions: By analyzing how donors engage with your site, you can optimize donation forms, increase conversion rates, and improve donor retention.
  • Identify Top Donors: Advanced reporting helps you identify your top donors, allowing you to develop personalized strategies for increasing their involvement and support.

lessons.title: 7. Peer-to-Peer Fundraising Platform Integration
lessons.content:
Tools: Classy, GiveWP, Zapier

How It Works:

  • Classy or GiveWP are peer-to-peer fundraising platforms that allow your supporters to create their own fundraising campaigns on your behalf.
  • Integrating these platforms with Zapier allows you to automatically update your CRM or email platform when a new peer fundraiser is created, or when donations come in from those campaigns.
  • You can trigger automated thank-you emails, notifications to the peer fundraiser, and real-time updates on their progress.

Example Growth Impact:

  • Expands Reach: Peer-to-peer fundraising allows your most engaged supporters to raise money on your behalf, expanding your reach to their networks.
  • Automated Engagement: Every time a donation is made to a peer fundraising campaign, the donor and the fundraiser can receive personalized thank-you messages, encouraging them to stay engaged.

lessons.title: 8. Website Chatbots for Donor and Volunteer Support
lessons.content:
Tools: Intercom, Drift, Zapier

How It Works:

  • Intercom or Drift can be used to set up chatbots on your non-profit’s website to assist visitors with frequently asked questions, event registrations, or donation inquiries.
  • Integrating these chat tools with Zapier allows the chatbot to automatically record conversations, add leads to your email list, and follow up with donors or volunteers.
  • For example, if someone asks how they can donate, the chatbot can guide them to a donation page and trigger a follow-up email with more information about your non-profit’s impact.

Example Growth Impact:

  • Improved Donor Experience: Visitors can get their questions answered immediately, without having to wait for staff. This can increase conversions from interested visitors to donors.
  • Volunteer Support: Volunteers can use the chatbot to sign up for events or get more information about available shifts, improving their engagement with your organization.

lessons.title: Summary of Technology Integration Benefits 🌐
lessons.content:
By integrating various technology platforms, non-profits can:

  • Automate time-consuming tasks, allowing staff to focus on mission-critical work.
  • Enhance donor and member engagement through personalized communication and seamless user experiences.
  • Streamline operations, reducing manual errors and improving efficiency.
  • Drive growth by expanding their reach through peer-to-peer fundraising and event automation.
